Translations.Title: Mixed numbers in the linear number system: Build the Idea
Translations.Explanation: This Cambridge Primary Stage 4 supporting lesson develops the open DfE Year 4 ready-to-progress focus “Mixed numbers in the linear number system”. Fractions describe equal parts and numbers on a number line. Equivalent fractions preserve value even when numerator and denominator change together. Build the idea by representing it in more than one way and explaining why the representations agree. The lesson is Edulytics-authored from OGL material; Cambridge remains the academic reference authority and no Cambridge objective wording is reproduced here.
Translations.KeyConceptsAndRules: Source focus: Mixed numbers in the linear number system. Fractions describe equal parts and numbers on a number line. Equivalent fractions preserve value even when numerator and denominator change together. Build the idea by representing it in more than one way and explaining why the representations agree. Always state what each number, unit, operation or geometric property represents before calculating.
Translations.WorkedExamples: Example A: Represent a fraction with equal parts, locate it on a number line and explain the role of the numerator and denominator. Explain each step and name the mathematical relationship being used. Example B: Use equivalence or a common denominator only when it helps compare or calculate without changing the value. Compare two possible approaches and choose the clearer one.
Translations.StepByStepSolutions: Step 1: Read the problem and identify the quantities or properties. Step 2: Represent the situation with numbers, a diagram, a number line, an equation or a labelled shape. Step 3: Apply the relevant rule while preserving place value, units and relationships. Step 4: Calculate carefully and write the result with its meaning. Step 5: Check using an inverse operation, estimation, an alternative representation or the stated geometric properties.
Translations.CommonMistakes: Do not add denominators when adding fractions, and do not assume a larger denominator means a larger fraction. Compare the value represented by the whole fraction. A correct-looking number is not enough if the representation or reasoning does not match the original relationship. Re-read the question and check units and magnitude.
Translations.QuickSummary: Mixed numbers in the linear number system: represent the idea clearly, apply the correct relationship, calculate accurately, and verify the result using a second line of reasoning.
